Bull case tomorrow: 7797-7800 is a very key zone. It was a resistance shelf from August 9th to August 13th. It broke out August 13th, and then last Thursday and Friday acted as support for the backtest. Then last evening, it failed, and we began a selloff. Remember sells in ES occur whenever a well-tested, previously defended support shelf collapses. Now, the bull case is simply that ES cant try to backtest this shelf. This would ideally involve ES holding 7716 (or quick trap below). 7738 reclaims are a possible long trigger en route. 7738 was a massive daily low from last Tuesday and its recovery is actionable.

3) Finally, while I discuss plenty of structures and levels above, its vital that we do not use any of the above to make predictions. Our job as traders is never to predict what price will do (literally impossible on an intraday basis). Our job is to plan zones, wait for price to present our setups at those zones, then manage the trade systematically level to level. I am not exagerating at all when I say the core difference between winning and losing traders is that losing traders are obssessed with knowing where price will go. Professionals don’t care - they let price pick the path and react. This allows one to trade what they see, not what they think, and not be affected by bias. When you predict, you are giving yourself a bias which blinds you from objectively trading the action. Price traps by its nature and takes the pathway engineered to cause the maximum pain to retail traders. You can pretend that it is a supercomputer that is intentionally trying to ensure that no retail traders profit from any large move, and ensure they are all stopped out, trapped, and frustrated before one occurs.

It is for this reason that instead of predicting the path and getting trapped non-stop, we need to flip the script and trade the traps: Wait on the Failed Breakdowns, manage profits level to level (thereby never predicting how far any move will go) and let runners work. Rinse and repeat daily. The second you start imagining price paths or trading on them, you’ve already lost the game.

Here is the difference in the types of statements professional traders make vs retail traders in this regard. A retail trader will make proclamations. They will say “We are going to sell 80 points, then rally 20, then sell another 100”. Or they say “We lost X leve, the top is in, we are heading lower”. Professionals say “If price tests X level, flushes it, and recovers, I long for a lvl to lvl move”. “If price rallies to Z level, I short for a level to level move”, “If price does none of the above, I do nothing”. Be a trader, not a fortune teller and don’t expect price to do anything. When I sit down to trade, I wipe my mind clean of any expectations, predictions, or opinions on direction. Have a plan for exactly where and how you want to engage, let price choose the path, then you can react accordingly. If your doing this right, you should be able to enter a session “feeling” the most bearish you have felt in a year, but if a Failed Breakdown triggers off the open, you are long. From there, all trades are managed systematically level to level, again never predicting how far any move will go.

With this in mind, let’s look at how yesterday’s execution plan applied to today’s action.

Trade Recap/Daily Summary

NOTE: The purpose of this trade recap section is to run down in greater detail previous examples of my three setup types that occurred within the last couple days. These setups are always provided to readers in advance, and the goal of this section is to expedite the lengthy screen time requirement that is associated with learning any trade setup. Trading is no different than learning a sport, or a musical instrument, or any other skill. You need to put in the reps - thousands of them. Unfortunately with trading, these reps are expensive. By showing examples of my three setups here everyday, the hope is readers can develop the pattern recognition quicker. The idea is that if there was a trade you were curious about or wanted more color on that occurred in the last couple days, you can scan through this section and hopefully I have identified it. Scroll to the next section for today’s action and the trade plan for tomorrow. Note that this section is also not exhaustive and I do not include every setup that occurred. When price is volatile, there may be many.

Tuesday Evening

The first high quality Failed Breakdown was the recovery of 7738. I wrote yesterday at 3pm: “7738 reclaims are a possible long trigger en route. 7738 was a massive daily low from last Tuesday and its recovery is actionable.”

Why is this a Failed Breakdown? A significant low has three possible definitions. 1) The prior days low 2) A multi-hour low/ a low that goes 20+ points or 3) A cluster or shelf of lows. At 7738 we had #1. 7738 was a prior days low, in particular the low of day from last Tuesday.

As always with Failed Breakdowns though the golden rule is if you just rush in long on the recovery of the significant low, you lose. Prior to entry you HAVE TO see either: 1) One of the two acceptance types. Acceptance is price action that we must see prior to entry, in order to prevent us from rushing in and getting trapped. It generally involves price trying to sell at or above the significant low then returning to it. By doing so, price is telling us that it wants to be there so that when we long the recovery of the significant low, we won’t rush in long, get trapped, and have price selloff. 2) The Non-Acceptance protocol. The non-acceptance protocol only triggers when price recovers the significant low (7738) by 5 points and holds above for a couple minutes. This typically triggers in high volatility, fast markets where price does not pause around the significant low (7738) and just rips through.

Remember 5 points above the significant low is the danger zone for Failed Breakdowns and where most losses occur. If entering in this zone you need clear acceptance and if you don’t see it or it is too noisy or uncertain, just wait for the non-acceptance protocol.

Remember the non-acceptance protocol automatically activates when price recovers the significant low (7738) by 5 points (7738+5=7743) and holds at or above 7743 for a few minutes. The non-acceptance protocol typically triggers for shallow (under 10 point flush of the significant low) and fast Failed Breakdowns, but you can use it for any Failed Breakdown. Typically I always use it when there is not clear, obvious, “jumps out at you” acceptance.

ES was far too weak to see this last evening, and simply continued to grind lower. We grinded down to 7704 by 830PM. The next available Failed Breakdown was the Failed Breakdown of 7716. I wrote yesterday at 3pm: “First support down is 7716. We set a nice shelf of lows there today. At 4am, we set a low there and bounced 20 points. At 11am, we also set a low around there and bounced again. The Failed Breakdown of this shelf is actionable. Bonus if we tag 7706 on this. While one could bid 7706, given bearish control I would never do this and would prefer to see it hold and recover 7716 to rally.”

ES bounced back to 7716 by 9pm and it acted as resistance all evening.

Wednesday Morning, the 7716 835AM Failed Breakdown, and Discussion on Acceptance

When I woke up and checked price at 730AM I noticed we were back at 7716 and ES spent all evening with 7716 as resistance. I would be prepared to long 7716 when the non-acceptance protocol triggers (7716+5=7721). As readers know, almost all my entries use the non-acceptance protocol lately. Acceptance typically becomes more present when we have deep Failed Breakdowns which we often see in more volatile markets. Lately, we just get shallow Failed Breakdowns where price may lose the low by 5 or 10 points then return to it and recover. It is hard to spot acceptance when there is this little room to work with without a microscope. Acceptance is more visible when we have very deep failed breakdowns. Price loses a low by 20, 3o, 40 points. Bounces back to it. Sells off, then returns to it again showing acceptance. Then we can long above.

We had this by 835AM hitting that 7721+ trigger, and I got long. This was managed as always: Locked in 75% profits at 7724 1st up, left 25% to run. Locked more at 7742 2nd up, left 10% to go.

This was all for today.

With a green trade in the books, this means its time for profit protection mode and time to let runners work and do absolutely nothing. As I often say I (and every other professional trader), don’t trade because the market is moving, because we are bored, because we have FOMO. We trade because a planned setup triggers at a planned zone, then the rest of the time is sitting there.

What does profit protection mode mean? This means after a win 1) I have to sit on the runner and do nothing all day, no other trades allowed. 2) I can take a second or third trade, only IF the runner stops out below break-even (or via a trailer if it is a larger rally where a trailing stop is involved), AND a new, pre-planned setup emerges. 3) I can take this second or third trade only risking the profits from the first, to ensure I have a green day. I take not going green to red on the day very seriously as do I take profit preservation very seriously.

I say this over and over everyday and I am intentionally repetitive about it since many new traders just don’t understand what day trading is. I trade in one hyper specific set of conditions only.

I need to see a vertical “elevator down” sell. Then I long when price flushes a low/shelf of lows for a Failed Breakdown. That is it. I don’t short, I don’t chase longs, I don’t flip back and forth long and short, I don’t trade chop, I don’t trade low vol, I don’t trade because some influencer posted a trade, I don’t trade because of news. I don’t care if price sells 500 points or 100 points - nothing to do with me. I don’t care what price is doing unless it is putting in an elevator down sell into a Failed Breakdown. This is day trading is. 99.9% of what you see on social media is just people gambling or engagement farming.

I am only ever doing 1 of two things: 1) I am waiting for an elevator down sell. 2) If there is no elevator down sell, I am simply riding my long runner from a previous trade with stop under previous days low. There is no other action or condition in which I trade.

I do the same template daily: I do 1-2 trades daily. These trades are typically before 11am, or after 3pm. I often enter between 730am and 830am, but this is not a hard rule. If there is no good entry in that morning window, I will enter later. I enter only at pre-planned, high conviction zones, on A+ setups. I rarely trade the window between 11am and 2pm as its often chop. First trade is a win in the morning, I hold the runner and I stop trading, only rarely trying one more in the afternoon. First trade is a loss, I trade one more. Both trades are losses, I quit for the day.

source_quote: Bear case tomorrow: Begins below 7695. These types of level loss shorts below a support are called breakdown trades. My core edge is failed breakdowns, and the reason is this is an edge is the vast majority of break downs (80%) trap. I do not take these trades personally. They take great skill to execute, and even when done well by a trader who has mastered these setups, one should expect over 60% to fail (they are low win rate, high R/R trades. 2 or 3 in a row will fail, then the 4th will pay out huge). *If you don’t like these odds and cant tolerate being trapped - simply don’t take them. I consider breakdown trades to be an advanced setup type so if a newer subscriber, there is nothing wrong with passing on these. For the 7695 short, ideally one can put in a final bounce or here, OR a Failed Breakdown then one can short beneath the lows of that bounce. Likely 7687 trigger down.
